subject: Urban Planning
title: Why Public Participation Matters
description: One-minute skill: Why Public Participation Matters.

hook.text: Jane Jacobs had no planning degree. She stopped Robert Moses by organizing her neighbors. Residents know best.

buildup.text: Top-down planning by experts failed repeatedly — Pruitt-Igoe, Brasília, highway demolitions. The experts were wrong.

discovery.text: Participatory planning invites residents to design their own neighborhoods. The results are messier but better.

twist.text: Public meetings are often dominated by wealthy homeowners. The people most affected are least likely to attend.

climax.text: Digital tools, multilingual outreach, and childcare at meetings are making participation more equitable.

punchline.text: Ask the people who live there. They know what they need.

quiz.question: Why do public planning meetings often fail to represent affected communities?
options: Residents don't care about planning decisions in their neighborhood
Wealthy homeowners dominate while those most affected are least likely to attend
Meetings are held in secret without any public notification
